It was during the second Covid lockdown. I lived alone, had lost my job, and hadn't seen another person in weeks except at the supermarket. I'd read that psilocybin could help with depression and I thought a big dose would be like years of therapy in one afternoon. I ordered dried mushrooms online and took about 4 grams on a Sunday, alone in my apartment, with a playlist I'd found online that was recommended for 'healing journeys'.

The first hour was emotional but okay. I cried about my job and my loneliness. Then the apartment started to feel like a cell. I realised, with a horrible clarity, that I was completely alone, not only in the apartment but in the world, and that nobody would notice if I disappeared. The music, which was meant to be uplifting, sounded hollow and mocking. I turned it off and the silence was worse.

I started to dissolve. I felt my sense of being a separate person melting into the walls of the apartment. I became the apartment, the empty rooms, the dust. Then even that went, and there was just a vast emptiness that had always been there and always would be. I understood that this emptiness was the real me, and that the person who'd had a job and friends was a mask over it. There was nothing to hold on to.

I don't know how long that lasted. When I came back a bit, I was lying on the kitchen floor. I didn't know how I got there. I tried to call someone, but I couldn't figure out how to use my phone. The screen was a mess of moving symbols. I gave up and lay there and watched the light change on the ceiling, convinced that I had permanently destroyed my self and that I'd be a hollow shell for the rest of my life.

Eventually it wore off. I slept for 14 hours. When I woke up, I felt like I was still on the kitchen floor in some way. I didn't tell anyone for months because there was nobody to tell.

Wir waren zu viert auf einem Segeltörn in Kroatien und hatten am dritten Tag beschlossen, in einer ruhigen Bucht LSD zu nehmen. Wir hatten nicht mit dem Wetter gerechnet. Am Nachmittag zog ein Sturm auf, und der Skipper, der als Einziger nüchtern war, entschied, dass wir die Bucht verlassen müssen, weil der Ankerplatz nicht sicher war.

Was dann kam, war der schlimmste Moment meines Lebens. Das Boot wurde von den Wellen hin und her geworfen, ich war seekrank und gleichzeitig auf dem Höhepunkt des Trips. Das Meer sah aus wie ein riesiges Maul, das uns verschlingen will. Ich war mir sicher, dass wir kentern und ertrinken. Ich habe mich an die Reling geklammert und mich übergeben und hatte das Gefühl, dass ich jeden Moment über Bord gehe. Ich hörte Stimmen im Wind, die mich riefen.

Der Skipper hat uns angeschrien, dass wir unter Deck gehen sollen, aber unten war es noch schlimmer, eng, dunkel, alles hat gewackelt und gerochen. Ich habe mich in eine Ecke gekauert und gebetet. Nach etwa zwei Stunden haben wir einen Hafen erreicht. Ich bin vom Boot gestolpert und habe mich auf den Steg gelegt und konnte nicht aufhören zu zittern. Die anderen waren auch fertig, aber ich glaube, mich hat es am schlimmsten erwischt.

Took 2C-E at a friend's place. The body load was awful. My heart was pounding and I felt like my veins were full of electricity, I couldn't sit still. I thought I was overdosing. Lasted for hours and I couldn't relax at all. My friend kept saying it would pass but it felt endless.

I'm a researcher and I volunteered for a phase 1 study of extended-state DMT, where DMT is given by continuous infusion so the experience lasts much longer than when you smoke it. I was screened, prepared, and I'd had experience with psychedelics before. I felt I was in the safest possible setting. I want to be clear that the study team was professional throughout.

The infusion started and within a minute I was gone. It was like being shot out of a cannon into another world. At first it was astonishing. Architectures of light, intelligences that seemed to welcome me. I remember thinking 'this is the most important moment of my life'.

But in a normal DMT experience you come back after 10-15 minutes. Here, I didn't come back. The world kept going. After what felt like a very long time, I began to lose track of the fact that I had a body or a life outside this place. The beings began to treat me as if I belonged there. One of them said, without words, that I had always been there, that the human life had been a short dream. And I believed it. I couldn't remember what 'human' meant.

Then a very deep terror set in. Not of the beings, but of the realisation that I would never wake up. That there was no 'outside'. That I had dissolved into this and there was nothing to go back to. I tried to remember my wife's face and couldn't. I tried to remember my name. There was nothing. Just an infinity of shifting patterns and a total absence of self. I wanted to scream but I had no mouth. The study protocol had a hand signal to stop the infusion, and I couldn't remember that I had hands.

The infusion lasted about 90 minutes in clock time. The study staff told me later that my vital signs were stable but that at some point my face showed visible distress, and they discussed stopping, but because I didn't give the signal and the protocol allowed for difficult experiences, they continued. I don't blame them.

When the infusion stopped and I came back, it was not a relief at first. It was like falling into a body that wasn't mine. The room, the researchers, the bed, all looked like a crude set. I didn't believe they were real. One of the researchers said my name and it sounded like a foreign word. It took about 30 minutes before I could speak coherently and maybe an hour before I felt like I was 'in' my life again. Even then I wasn't fully sure.

I did the post-session interview, and I tried to describe what happened, but I don't think I conveyed the horror of it. I went home that evening. My wife picked me up and I looked at her for a long time trying to decide if she was real.

I'm 68 and was diagnosed with prostate cancer two years ago. I'd read about psilocybin helping cancer patients with fear of death. Legal trials weren't available where I live, so I found a 'guide' through an acquaintance. He came to my house with a large dose of mushrooms. I took them in my living room.

It started fine. I felt peaceful and was thinking about my grandchildren. Then I got very confused. I didn't know where I was, I couldn't understand the guide's words, and I got very frightened that I was dying right then, from the cancer. I tried to stand up to find my wife, who was out shopping, and I fell and hit my hip on the coffee table. The pain was enormous but in the trip it felt like the cancer had broken through my bones. The guide panicked and didn't know what to do. He didn't want to call an ambulance because of the mushrooms. He waited until my wife came home an hour later, and she called one. I had a hairline fracture of the hip. In the hospital I was still disoriented and the nurses thought I had dementia.

Wir waren auf einem Festival, als in der Nacht ein heftiges Unwetter kam. Ich hatte LSD genommen und lag im Zelt, als der Sturm das Zelt eingerissen hat. Plötzlich war alles nass, kalt und laut, der Boden war ein einziger Schlammsee. Ich konnte im Dunkeln nichts sehen und habe den Ausgang nicht gefunden. Ich hatte das Gefühl, im Schlamm zu ertrinken, und habe um mich geschlagen. Überall um mich herum haben Menschen geschrien, und der Donner war so laut, dass ich dachte, die Welt geht unter. Ich habe mich an einen Pfosten geklammert und bin bis zum Morgen nicht losgekommen. Ich habe meine Freunde erst am nächsten Mittag wiedergefunden.

I was in my first year at college and took LSD in my dorm with my roommate and a few people from our floor. I'd never done it before. A couple of hours in, I got very emotional and started crying about my parents' divorce, and then I started talking to the wall, because I thought it was alive and was listening to me. I was saying very personal things, about my dad, about being lonely, about a girl I liked. I didn't realise that one of the guys was filming me on his phone.

Later in the trip I became very paranoid. I thought everyone was laughing at me, and I was right, they were. I saw them looking at the phone and giggling. I asked what they were watching and they hid it. I felt completely exposed and humiliated, like my soul had been put on display. I went into the bathroom and stayed there for hours, looking at myself in the mirror and seeing my face distort into something ugly.

The next day the video was in a group chat with about 200 people from our dorm. It spread from there. People I didn't know were quoting the things I said to the wall. Someone made a meme. The girl I mentioned saw it. For weeks I couldn't walk across campus without someone saying one of my lines and laughing.

The trip itself was frightening, but the worst part was realising that people I thought were friends had done this.
Ayahuasca ceremony. I saw the man who abused me as a child sitting across from me in the circle. He was smiling. I knew he wasn't really there, but I also knew he was. I froze for hours.

Ich bin vor drei Jahren nach Brasilien gereist, um an einem zweiwöchigen Ayahuasca-Retreat teilzunehmen. Ich hatte vorher schon zwei Zeremonien in Europa gemacht und fühlte mich gut vorbereitet. Das Retreat lag abgelegen im Wald, ungefähr vier Stunden von der nächsten Stadt entfernt.

In der dritten Nacht ist etwas Furchtbares passiert. Ein Teilnehmer, ein Mann aus den USA, etwa Mitte fünfzig, hat während der Zeremonie plötzlich laut gestöhnt und ist dann zusammengesackt. Zuerst dachten alle, das sei Teil seines Prozesses. Die Begleiter haben gesagt, er arbeite mit der Medizin. Ich lag nur ein paar Meter entfernt und war selbst mitten in sehr starken Visionen. Ich habe gesehen, wie sein Körper sich verfärbt hat, und ich hatte das Gefühl, dass der Tod im Raum ist, als dunkle Gestalt, die über ihm schwebt.

Irgendwann haben die Begleiter gemerkt, dass er nicht mehr atmet. Dann brach Chaos aus. Leute haben geschrien, das Licht wurde angemacht, jemand hat versucht, ihn wiederzubeleben. Ich habe das alles gesehen, durch einen Schleier aus Farben und Mustern, und ich wusste nicht, was echt ist. Ich habe gedacht, dass ich die Nächste bin, dass in der Medizin etwas Giftiges war und wir alle sterben werden. Mein Herz raste, ich bekam keine Luft.

Es dauerte über eine Stunde, bis ein Wagen kam, um ihn abzuholen. Wir mussten die ganze Zeit in der Hütte bleiben. Es gab keinen Arzt, kein Telefonnetz. Er lag dort, unter einer Decke, und ich konnte nicht aufhören, hinzuschauen. Ich habe gesehen, wie sein Gesicht unter der Decke zu einem Totenkopf wurde. Ich habe mich übergeben und konnte mich nicht bewegen.

Später haben wir erfahren, dass er an einem Herzproblem gestorben ist, möglicherweise in Verbindung mit einem Medikament, das er genommen hatte. Das Retreat wurde abgebrochen. Ich bin mit den anderen am nächsten Tag in die Stadt gefahren, ohne geschlafen zu haben, und dann sofort nach Hause geflogen. Auf dem ganzen Flug habe ich sein Gesicht gesehen.
DMT. Saw god and god was furious with me. I was terrified for maybe 10 minutes.

I was at a warehouse rave, on LSD and a bit of MDMA. My friend Sam was also taking GHB, which I didn't know. Around 3am I found him slumped in a corner, not responding. His lips were blue and his breathing was very slow and weird. I was tripping hard and I couldn't tell if it was real or a hallucination. I shook him and he didn't wake up. I screamed for help and a couple of people came over and one of them knew first aid and said he wasn't breathing properly.

Someone called an ambulance. The first aider started rescue breathing and told me to keep talking to Sam. I held his hand and talked to him and I was convinced he was dead and that his soul was floating out of his body. I could see it, like a grey mist rising. The music was still pounding and the strobe was going and I was in hell.

The paramedics took him away. I wasn't allowed in the ambulance. I sat outside on the pavement until dawn, not knowing if he was alive. My phone died. I walked home, which took two hours, seeing his blue face in every shop window.

Sam survived. He was in intensive care for two days. When I finally visited him he was fine and joked about it.

Ich habe mehrmals an einem Abend Salvia geraucht, weil es so kurz wirkt. Beim dritten Mal bin ich in eine Welt gekommen, in der ich ein Teil einer riesigen Maschine war, die sich immer gleich bewegt. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass ich schon seit Millionen Jahren dort bin und nie wieder wegkomme. Als ich zurückkam, war ich mir nicht sicher, ob mein Leben echt ist oder ob ich gleich wieder in die Maschine gezogen werde.
